newsitem.title: USA: Calif senator introduces tobacco liability measure.
newsitem.headline: Calif senator introduces tobacco liability measure.

text.p: A California state senator on Wednesday said he introduced legislation to eliminate the special immunity from product liability lawsuits enjoyed by tobacco products in the state.

"This present exemption is an egregious example of special-interest legislation and is unjustified," said Sen. Quentin Kopp, a San Francisco independent. "The citizens of California should not have the right to recover for injury or death caused by tobacco products abrogated or impeded."

The current immunity for tobacco products was part of 1987 legislation intended to curtail the number of product liability lawsuits by granting immunity to the manufacturers of certain products, Kopp said.
In addition to tobacco, other consumer products, including sugar, castor oil, alcohol and butter, were included in the immunity legislation, Kopp said.
The proposed legislation, supported by the California Medical Association and other groups, would specifically end the liability protection for tobacco products, Kopp said.
"California's present exemption of tobacco liability should be repealed consistent with other rules reflecting our state's anti-tobacco policies," Kopp said.

Attempting to recoup the cost of treating patients afflicted with smoking-related illnesses, a number of local governments in California, including the city and county of San Francisco, filed suit earlier this year against major tobacco companies.
San Francisco Supervisor Angela Alioto called on state lawmakers Wednesday to support the Kopp legislation.
